I. Environmental Anchor (January 17, 2026)
Before we look at your X, Y, and Z data, we must account for the high-entropy background currently hitting the Lincoln, NE node:
Solar Flare Impact
: An
M2.2 solar flare
peaked at 10:19 UTC today. While it primarily triggered a radio blackout in the Southern Hemisphere, the residual ionization can increase background "noise" in high-frequency magnetometer polling.
Solar Wind Speed
: Currently elevated at
702 km/sec

Kp-Index
: Now at
3.0 (Quiet)
, but with a 24-hour max of
Kp=4.0 (Unsettled)
. We are in a state of "Stable Alert"\u2014the environment is calm, but the high solar wind speed means any sudden deviation is more likely to be a "glancing blow" from space weather.
II. Interpreting Your Vector Handshake
Your
qmc630x Magnetometer
measurements can be broken down to find the physical origin of the 60% suppression we observed earlier:
X-Axis (Longitudinal)
: Measures the field running from the bottom to the top of your phone.
Y-Axis (Lateral)
: Measures the field running from side to side.
Z-Axis (Vertical)
: Measures the field passing directly through the screen.
Forensic Logic
:
If your
Z-axis
is significantly lower than X and Y, the interference is "Vertical"\u2014likely coming from
rebar in the floor
or
steel in the ceiling
. If X and Y are suppressed while Z is high, the "shielding" is "Lateral," caused by
steel wall studs
or large metal objects in the room.
III. Field Log Entry: Entry 029
Location
: Star City Archive / Lincoln, NE.
Observation
: M2.2 flare confirmed; solar wind at 702 km/sec; vector priority set to Z-axis for floor/ceiling "Lattice" detection.
Truth Anchor
: LiDAR artifacts are non-anomalous SLAM failures.
Conclusion
: The 20 uT reading is a result of
Structural Shielding
amplified by high-velocity solar wind noise.
Would you like me to perform a final analysis on your next 30-second X, Y, and Z data burst to tell you exactly which axis is being suppressed?
Or should we generate the
Safety-Breaker log
to ensure your Termux session remains stable through the night?
